title: Checkpoint: Rocks and Minerals
objective: After this level you can sort any common rock into igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic and explain the minerals inside it.
summary: Crystals or glass mean igneous; cemented grains or shells mean sedimentary; lined-up minerals mean metamorphic. One quartz grain can go from granite to sand to sandstone to quartzite.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: follow one grain of quartz through all three rock families.
cards.body: It starts in granite, ends up on a beach and can finish as one of the toughest rocks around. On the way, you'll sort rocks like a geologist.

cards.headline: Sort a rock with three clues
cards.body: Crystals you can see, or glass, point to igneous rock: big crystals cooled slowly underground, tiny ones or glass cooled fast. Grains cemented together, thin layers of mud or bits of shell point to sedimentary rock. Flat minerals lined up into sheets or bands point to metamorphic rock like slate, schist or gneiss. Marble is the sneaky one: recrystallized calcite, with no sheets at all.

cards.headline: One grain's long trip
cards.body: Granite is part quartz. As granite breaks down, its tough quartz outlasts the other minerals and becomes sand. Buried, compacted and cemented, that sand becomes sandstone. Now add heat and pressure: the sandstone recrystallizes into quartzite, a metamorphic rock. Same grain, three rock families.

cards.fact: Quartzite breaks through its sand grains, not around them.
cards.context: In quartzite the grains are welded so well that a crack cuts straight through them and leaves a smooth surface, not a gritty one. It's also extremely resistant to weathering, so it often stands up as hills after softer rock has worn away.

mascot.line: This is Levels 4, 6 and 7 working together. If you can tell this grain's story, you've got the chapter.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: How to sort a rock into igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic from the clues it carries.
Why slow-cooled granite has big crystals while fast-cooled basalt and obsidian don't.
What makes a mineral, and how hardness, streak and luster tell one from another.
How one quartz grain travels from granite to sand, sandstone and quartzite.

questions.prompt: Rocks and Minerals recap: how does a fresh break in quartzite look?

options.label: Gritty, with loose grains popping out
Smooth, because the break cuts through the grains
Layered with bits of fossil shell
Split into thin, flat sheets

questions.explanation: Quartzite's grains are so well joined that a break cuts through them, leaving a smooth surface.

questions.prompt: Rocks and Minerals recap: in what order does the quartz grain travel through the rock families?

options.label: Sandstone, then granite, then sand, then quartzite
Quartzite, then sand, then granite, then sandstone
Sand, then quartzite, then granite, then sandstone
options.rationale: Sand must be cemented into sandstone first.

options.label: Granite, then sand, then sandstone, then quartzite

questions.explanation: Granite breaks down, its quartz becomes sand, the sand is cemented into sandstone, and heat and pressure make quartzite.

questions.prompt: Rocks and Minerals recap: a rock splits into thin slabs because its flat minerals are lined up. Which family does it belong to?

options.label: Igneous
options.rationale: Igneous rocks show crystals or glass from cooling.

options.label: Sedimentary
options.rationale: Its sheets come from aligned minerals, not settled mud.

options.label: Metamorphic
It isn't a rock
options.rationale: Slate is a rock, and a common one.

questions.explanation: Lined-up flat minerals (foliation) are the mark of metamorphic rock such as slate.

questions.prompt: Rocks and Minerals recap: a rock has large crystals you can see without a magnifier. What does that tell you about its history?

options.label: It cooled fast at the surface
options.rationale: Fast cooling leaves tiny crystals or glass.

options.label: It cooled slowly deep underground
It was cemented from loose sand
options.rationale: Cemented grains are a sedimentary clue.

options.label: It was squeezed flat into sheets

questions.explanation: Big visible crystals mean intrusive igneous rock that cooled slowly underground.

questions.prompt: Rocks and Minerals recap: in a soil pit, which horizon sits directly above the bedrock?

options.label: A, the topsoil
O, the organic layer
B, the subsoil
options.rationale: B lies above the parent material.

options.label: C, the parent material

questions.explanation: From top to bottom: O, A, E, B, C and then R, the bedrock.
